panels.title: Status
panels.description: DUX3-11: Selected-provider HEALTH only when provider is selected. Empty provider → N/A (not green zero success). Selected-range provider-first severity for the selected provider. Status mapping: 0=OK, 1=WARN, >=2=CRIT, null=UNKNOWN. Uses bioetl_provider_current_status and bioetl_provider_range_operational_ok inside the active Grafana time range (default Last 12 hours). Operational OK is projected when health-check or adapter request counters show successful provider activity without failures or HTTP errors in range; it does not prove the currently selected pipeline run succeeded, but it prevents UNKNOWN after successful provider operations in range. If both series are absent, UNKNOWN remains fail-closed; inspect Monitor Provider Telemetry Freshness and Review Raw Provider Health Enum. Pipeline/run_type/workflow are secondary context only; run_id does not filter Prometheus. This compact Status is selected-provider scope and is intentionally rendered as a supporting selected-provider verdict, not as the visual owner of the fleet answer. GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix and Critical Providers are global fleet posture and may disagree by design. Do not compare the selected-provider OK card to a GLOBAL WARN/CRIT panel without reading the scope labels. DSA-06: freshness-aware fleet vs selected.

panels.title: First Action
panels.description: DUX3-22: Start GLOBAL fleet matrix + freshness before selected-provider detail. Population-first CTA. Start with GLOBAL severity and top causes before selected-provider scope. Empty top causes with non-OK severity is an explainability gap, not a healthy signal. First operator CTA for global provider incidents and early-warning provider causes. Start with the current GLOBAL severity matrix, then telemetry freshness, then critical providers and top causes. Treat selected-provider Status as supporting scoped evidence; if Status is UNKNOWN, treat that as missing provider-current-status evidence until telemetry freshness and raw enum evidence say otherwise. Use this after the current answer row; selected-range latency/error evidence stays below and downstream Runtime or Control Plane follow-up depends on the diagnosed cause. Phase-2 CTA standard. Empty causes with non-OK severity is an explainability gap. DSA-06: current fleet triage with freshness; optional latency collapsed.

options.content:
**Dependency Health — next actions (<=4)**
1. Read **Status** with **Telemetry Freshness** (blind spot vs confirmed degradation).
2. Open worst row in **Severity Matrix** / **Critical Providers**.
3. Confirm **Top Causes** (VALID_EMPTY only if Status=OK and freshness healthy).
4. Affected run identity -> **Run Explorer**; multi-domain -> **Incident**.

panels.description: GLOBAL provider severity matrix. Scope: GLOBAL provider fleet posture; intentionally not filtered by run_id. Interpret with freshness: critical -> degraded -> unknown/stale -> healthy. No data + UNKNOWN Status = blind spot, not empty healthy fleet.
panels.title: Monitor GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix

panels.description: Only providers currently observed as DEGRADED or FAILING on the first-screen provider-status recording rule (instant/current semantics, not selected-range history). Empty table means no provider is currently above OK in the active trust window. Scope: GLOBAL provider fleet posture; intentionally not filtered by run_id. Fleet-first matrix: answer without forcing a provider selector; select row to deep-dive.
panels.title: Inspect Critical Providers

panels.description: Canonical provider cause projection from bioetl_provider_current_cause. Top provider causes using current/instant selectors (not selected-range history): raw status, failure rate, retry exhaustion, latency, HTTP errors, or rate-limit pressure. Scope: GLOBAL provider fleet posture; intentionally not filtered by run_id. Population-first fleet evidence (not selected-provider only). Empty table while GLOBAL severity is non-OK is an explainability gap — check scrape/rules (DUX-09). Fleet-first matrix: answer without forcing a provider selector; select row to deep-dive. DSA-06: VALID_EMPTY only when Status=OK and freshness healthy.

defaults.noValue: VALID_EMPTY — no current causes (check Status/freshness if non-OK)

panels.title: Inspect Provider Top Causes

panels.description: DUX3-11: Freshness is EVIDENCE confidence. STALE/MISSING reduces trust; does not prove provider OK. Current provider telemetry freshness marker for the first screen (instant status). Status mapping: 0=OK, 1=WARN, >=2=CRIT, null=UNKNOWN. Missing bioetl_provider_current_status remains fail-closed UNKNOWN, not OK. UNKNOWN — provider freshness marker absent. DSA-06: freshness reduces confidence when stale.
panels.title: Monitor Provider Telemetry Freshness

panels.description: Conditional selected-provider latency/retry trends. Collapsed until needed; not first-screen when selector empty (DSA-06).
panels.title: Selected Provider Detail
Track Failure and Degraded Trend by Provider
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: failure/degraded probe trend over the active Grafana interval.

panels.title: Track Provider Failure Share (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: provider share of failed probes in the active Grafana range. The full share chart is collapsed by default and should be expanded only when total failures are non-zero.

panels.title: Track Retries Exhausted by Provider/Operation
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: retries exhausted by provider and operation in the active Grafana range. Non-zero rows identify where retry budgets were consumed, not raw provider-health enum state.

panels.title: Track Retries Exhausted Trend by Provider/Operation
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: retry exhaustion trend by provider and operation over the active Grafana interval. Rising non-zero series point to persistent retry-budget pressure.

defaults.noValue: No optional health-check latency samples in range; not a provider verdict.

panels.title: Inspect Provider Health Check Latency (p95) - $provider
panels.description: DUX4-12: Empty state must describe latency samples (not circuit-breaker trips). Compact optional selected-range evidence: per-provider p95 health-check latency over the active Grafana range. No data means no latency samples or no probe activity in range, not 0s latency and not a provider verdict.

defaults.noValue: No optional adapter latency samples in range; not a provider verdict.

panels.title: Inspect Adapter Request Latency by Endpoint (p95)
panels.description: DUX4-12: Empty state must describe latency samples (not circuit-breaker trips). Compact optional selected-range evidence: p95 adapter request latency by endpoint for the selected provider scope. Provider-global selected-range only; for backfill-specific stage latency open 2. Runtime with preserved pipeline/run_type/run_id scope. No data remains diagnostic and means no endpoint latency samples in range; it does not refute current provider severity.

defaults.noValue: No optional rate-limit error samples in range; not a provider verdict.

targets.expr: round(sum by (provider, method, error_type) (increase(bioetl_http_request_errors_total{provider=~"$provider", error_type=~"(?i).*(rate.?limit|429|thrott).*"}[$__interval])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Inspect Rate Limit Errors by Method
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range rate-limit pressure from HTTP errors where error_type indicates throttling/rate-limit classes. Empty samples stay diagnostic and do not refute current provider severity. Use alongside Monitor Rate Limiter Wait p95 for provider-global scope.

defaults.noValue: No optional timeout/network samples in range; not a provider verdict.

targets.expr: round(sum by (provider, method, error_type) (increase(bioetl_http_request_errors_total{provider=~"$provider", error_type=~"(?i).*(timeout|timed.?out|network).*"}[$__interval])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Inspect Network Timeout Errors by Method
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range network/timeout failures separated from rate-limit pressure. Empty samples stay diagnostic and do not refute current provider severity. Provider-global scope; correlate with Runtime stage errors when pipeline handoff context is set.

defaults.noValue: No optional rate-limiter wait samples in range; not a provider verdict.

panels.title: Track Rate Limiter Wait by Provider (p95)
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range evidence: p95 wait time imposed by provider rate limiting. No data means no observed wait samples in range, not a healthy wait time. This optional telemetry can stay empty even when current provider severity is non-OK. The provider degraded-rule surface starts at p95 > 1s; this panel keeps a lower yellow band for earlier-warning inspection.

defaults.noValue: No rate-limiter token samples in range. This remains diagnostic and does not disprove provider pressure.

panels.title: Monitor Minimum Rate Limiter Tokens Available
panels.description: Compact optional selected-range evidence: minimum provider tokens available in the active Grafana range. Lower values indicate higher rate-limit pressure; 0 means requests can be blocked. No data remains diagnostic and means no token samples were observed in range. This optional telemetry can stay empty even when current provider severity is non-OK.

defaults.noValue: No circuit-breaker state samples in range. Adapter-scoped telemetry is optional and does not imply CLOSED.

panels.title: Monitor Cross-Scope Adapter Circuit Breaker State (max)
panels.description: Compact cross-scope adapter diagnostics over the active Grafana range: 0=CLOSED, 1=HALF_OPEN, 2=OPEN. Uses the adapter selector because the shipped metric family is adapter-labelled rather than provider-labelled. No data remains diagnostic and does not imply a synthetic CLOSED state. This adapter-scoped telemetry can stay empty even when current provider severity is non-OK.

defaults.noValue: No circuit-breaker trip samples in range. Adapter-scoped telemetry is optional and remains diagnostic.

panels.title: Track Cross-Scope Adapter Circuit Breaker Trips
panels.description: Compact cross-scope adapter diagnostics: selected-range circuit-breaker trip count by adapter over the active Grafana interval. This panel is intentionally adapter-scoped because the shipped metric family is adapter-labelled rather than provider-labelled. No data remains diagnostic and does not create synthetic adapter rows. Empty adapter telemetry does not refute current provider severity on its own.

panels.title: Review Raw Provider Health Enum
panels.description: Raw provider health enum evidence for the current first-screen scope (instant), not the canonical first-screen verdict. Values are source enum: 0=UNHEALTHY, 1=DEGRADED, 2=HEALTHY (or dashboard-local mapping). null/NaN=UNKNOWN when raw status is absent (mapping fallback), not healthy. When raw status is absent the mapped status is unknown (fail-closed), never synthetic healthy.

defaults.noValue: No provider latency samples in range. This optional telemetry is neutral; use severity, freshness, and raw enum panels for provider verdict.

panels.title: Track Health Check Latency by Provider (p95)
panels.description: DUX4-12: Empty state must describe latency samples (not circuit-breaker trips). Selected-range evidence: p95 provider health-check latency over the active Grafana interval. Current provider severity is owned by the GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix.

panels.title: Monitor Healthy Checks (Selected Range)
panels.description: DUX4-12: Denominator 0 → N/A/SELECTION_REQUIRED, never green success 0.00%. DUX3-11/03: Ratios with denominator 0 must render N/A or VALID_EMPTY — never green success 0.00%. Selected-range evidence: completed HEALTHY probes in the active Grafana range. This panel is not a current-health source.

panels.title: Monitor Degraded Checks (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: completed DEGRADED probes in the active Grafana range. This panel is not a current-health source, so non-zero counts remain neutral evidence rather than WARN/CRIT by themselves.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_success_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_degraded_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: Track Provider Failure Rate (Selected Range)
panels.description: DUX4-12: Denominator 0 → N/A/SELECTION_REQUIRED, never green success 0.00%. DUX3-11/03: Ratios with denominator 0 must render N/A or VALID_EMPTY — never green success 0.00%. Selected-range evidence: failed probes divided by completed probes in the active Grafana range. Current status comes from bioetl_provider_current_status. Gauge thresholds follow the provider policy contract: warning at 5%, critical at 20%. A 0.00% value is neutral supporting evidence and never renders as a dominant red gauge arc.

targets.expr: round((sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_success_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_degraded_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)))

panels.title: Track Health Checks Total (Selected Range)
panels.description: DUX4-12: Denominator 0 → N/A/SELECTION_REQUIRED, never green success 0.00%. DUX3-11/03: Ratios with denominator 0 must render N/A or VALID_EMPTY — never green success 0.00%. Selected-range evidence: total completed provider health checks in the active Grafana range.

panels.title: Run context (thin) -> Run Explorer hub
ID
panels.description: Compact two-column local control-plane identity table. Shows Run ID, Manifest ID, Provider.Entity [Version], Contract [Schema], Execution, execution flags, Replay [Capability.Mode], Checkpoint [Anchors], optional Composite Run, and Identity Health. Exact selected run_id wins; aggregate pipeline scope without exact run_id must not guess one manifest identity; values come from HTTP, not Prometheus labels. This card is bounded pipeline/run context evidence only and does not prove current provider health. No data/datasource errors on this HTTP-backed card mean the BioETL Ops HTTP/control-plane backend may be unavailable; verify /health/live before interpreting the card as expected empty. Fail-closed: timeout, empty, or unresolved identity/accounting must render UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE/NO DATA — never a synthetic healthy zero. DSA-04: thin shell; canonical hub Run Explorer.

defaults.noValue: Not resolved — no identity rows for the selected run/scope. Check backend health (/health/live), then select or reset run_id; this is not a valid empty run.

panels.title: Processed Records
panels.description: Current stage/outcome accounting evidence for the shared pipeline/run_type context. Provider remains the primary health selector; this table is bounded pipeline/run_type accounting evidence and does not prove current provider health by itself. Missing accounting series render UNKNOWN/no data, not OK. Summary status, accounted subtotal, and delta rows are intentionally not displayed in this compact table; use Status, Monitor Provider Telemetry Freshness, and detailed recording rules for verdict/delta triage. No data/datasource errors on this HTTP-backed card mean the BioETL Ops HTTP/control-plane backend may be unavailable; verify /health/live before interpreting the card as expected empty. Fail-closed: timeout, empty, or unresolved identity/accounting must render UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE/NO DATA — never a synthetic healthy zero. DSA-04: thin shell; canonical hub Run Explorer.

defaults.noValue: Not resolved — no processed-record rows. Check backend health and selector scope; backend unavailable is not a valid zero-record state.

panels.description: DUX4-23: Collapsed by default — Run Explorer owns first-class ID/Processed Records. DUX3-26: Collapsed thin shell only. Canonical ID/Processed Records hub is Run Explorer. DUX3-26: Collapsed thin shell; Run Explorer is the hub.
